es: Reconocer las partes de un plan de negocio (resumen, mercado, marketing, operaciones, finanzas, riesgos, equipo) y el lenguaje típico de cada una.

teaching.en: The executive summary opens a business plan in a few lines: what the workshop will do, for whom, and why it should succeed.
teaching.es: El resumen ejecutivo abre un plan de negocio en pocas líneas: qué hará el taller, para quién y por qué debería tener éxito.
teaching.explanationEs: Es la sección más leída; debe poder entenderse sin leer el resto del plan.
segments: The executive summary opens a business plan in a few lines: what
the workshop will do, for whom, and why it should succeed.
teaching.audioText: The executive summary opens a business plan in a few lines: what the workshop will do, for whom, and why it should succeed.

teaching.en: The market section names the target market and the competitors already serving it, and explains what makes the newcomer different.
teaching.es: La sección de mercado nombra el mercado objetivo y a los competidores que ya lo atienden, y explica qué hace diferente al recién llegado.
teaching.explanationEs: Fíjate en los grupos de clientes y en las comparaciones con otros negocios.
segments: The market section names the target market and the competitors
already serving it, and explains what makes the newcomer different.
teaching.audioText: The market section names the target market and the competitors already serving it, and explains what makes the newcomer different.

teaching.en: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.
teaching.es: El marketing explica cómo se dará a conocer la empresa; las operaciones describen los turnos y proveedores que sostienen el trabajo diario.
teaching.explanationEs: Marketing usa will + verbo base; operations habla de horarios, turnos y rutinas.
segments: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations
describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.
teaching.audioText: Marketing explains how the firm will promote itself; operations describe the shifts and suppliers behind the daily work.

teaching.en: Finance asks for a loan, tracks cash flow month by month and shows when the business should break even.
teaching.es: Finanzas pide un préstamo, sigue el flujo de caja mes a mes y muestra cuándo debería alcanzar el negocio el punto de equilibrio.
teaching.explanationEs: Break even es alcanzar el punto en que los ingresos igualan a los costes; el beneficio llega después.
segments: Finance asks for a loan, tracks cash flow month by
month and shows when the business should break even.
teaching.audioText: Finance asks for a loan, tracks cash flow month by month and shows when the business should break even.

teaching.en: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.
teaching.es: Toda previsión de beneficio se apoya en supuestos, así que un plan creíble los declara abiertamente en lugar de esconderlos en una tabla.
teaching.explanationEs: Los números sin supuestos explícitos suenan más seguros de lo que son.
segments: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan
states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.
teaching.audioText: Every forecast of profit rests on assumptions, so a credible plan states them openly instead of hiding them in a table.

teaching.en: The risk section names what may go wrong; the team section shows that a skilled mechanic can deal with it.
teaching.es: La sección de riesgos nombra lo que puede salir mal; la del equipo muestra que un mecánico con experiencia puede afrontarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Riesgos usa may para lo posible pero incierto; el equipo presenta experiencia y funciones.
segments: The risk section names what may go wrong; the team
section shows that a skilled mechanic can deal with it.
teaching.audioText: The risk section names what may go wrong; the team section shows that a skilled mechanic can deal with it.

prompt.es: ¿A qué sección pertenece este fragmento y por qué?

choices.text: Marketing: it explains how customers will hear about the workshop.
Market: it describes who the customers are and who else serves them.
Operations: it sets out the daily routine of the workshop.

feedback.es: Habla de cómo darse a conocer (promote) y de una oferta para atraer clientes: es marketing, no descripción del mercado.

hint.es: Busca el verbo promote: explica cómo darse a conocer.

origin.text: We will promote the workshop through local cycling clubs and a weekly offer for students, and we will measure each campaign by the number of new customers it brings.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nuestro mercado objetivo son estudiantes y trabajadores que van en bici.»

feedback.es: Target market es el grupo de clientes al que se dirige el negocio; aparece en la sección de mercado.

origin.text: Our ___ market is made up of students and workers who cycle every day, and the two competitors in the area ignore them at weekends.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Necesitamos un préstamo para comprar herramientas y pagar el alquiler.»

answer.text: We need a loan to buy tools and pay the rent

feedback.es: La frase pertenece a finanzas: need a loan + to + verbo indica para qué se pide el dinero.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fragmento con la sección del plan a la que pertenece.

pairs: Leo has ten years of experience as a mechanic and has led a team of six.
Each mechanic will work one morning shift and one afternoon shift.
Posters in local cafes and a weekly offer will attract new customers.
Most of our customers are students under thirty who cycle every day.
If costs rise faster than sales, we may have to raise our prices.

feedback.es: Cada fragmento usa el lenguaje de su sección: experiencia, turnos, promoción, clientes y posibles problemas.

pairs: Leo has ten years of experience as a mechanic and has led a team of six.
Each mechanic will work one morning shift and one afternoon shift.
Posters in local cafes and a weekly offer will attract new customers.
Most of our customers are students under thirty who cycle every day.
If costs rise faster than sales, we may have to raise our prices.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué sección procede este fragmento y cómo lo sabes.

choices.text: Marketing: it explains how the firm will make itself known to the public.
Market: it describes the customers and what the competitors do not offer.
Operations: it sets out opening hours and shifts for each worker.

feedback.es: Se habla de clientes y de competidores que no abren los domingos: es la sección de mercado.

origin.audio: Our main customers are commuters who ride to work, and two competitors already repair bicycles in the area. Neither of them opens on Sundays, and that is the chance we intend to take.

prompt.es: Completa: «Esperamos alcanzar el punto de equilibrio en nueve meses.»

feedback.es: Break even significa llegar al punto en que los ingresos cubren los costes; después llega el beneficio.

origin.text: The plan shows cash flow month by month. We expect to ___ even after nine months, and to make a profit from then on.

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el posible socio sobre este plan?

choices.text: That the executive summary is too vague, so the authors should rewrite it before meeting.
That the risk section is wrong and the market section should be left exactly as it stands.
That two sections seem to disagree with each other and must be made to agree.
That he will not meet the authors until the loan they are asking for has been reduced.

feedback.es: El socio señala que el mercado dice una cosa y los riesgos otra, y pide que las dos secciones concuerden antes de reunirse.

origin.text: A note from a possible partner: The plan is well written, and the executive summary is clear. However, the market section claims that nobody else serves cyclists, while the risk section admits that two competitors already repair bicycles nearby. Either the market has been overstated or the risks have been understated. I would like the authors to make the two sections agree before we meet.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase del plan pertenece a la sección de riesgos.

choices.text: The one about customers who may leave if prices go up.
The one about the loan for tools and rent.
The one about reaching the break-even point after nine months.

feedback.es: Los dos primeros enunciados describen dinero que entra o sale (finanzas); el tercero, sobre clientes que podrían marcharse si suben los precios, es algo que podría salir mal: va en riesgos.

origin.audio: I am checking where each sentence of my business plan belongs, and my partner is helping me. The first says that we need a loan of twelve thousand dollars, which would cover tools and the first three months of rent. The second says that we expect to break even after nine months. My partner points out that those two belong together, because both describe money that comes in or goes out. The last sentence warns that customers might leave if we raise our prices. That one needs a heading of its own, since it is neither a figure nor a promise, but something that could go wrong. I will move each sentence to its right section tonight, and then I will read the whole plan again from the top.

prompt.es: Completa: «El resumen ejecutivo debe sintetizar todo el plan en una sola página.»

feedback.es: Summarise es el verbo preciso para condensar un plan entero en una página.

origin.text: The executive summary should ___ the whole plan on a single page: what the business does, who it serves and why it will work.

prompt.es: Escribe la sección de mercado de una panadería nueva: clientes y competidores.

answer.text: Our target market is office workers who want fresh bread before eight in the morning. Two competitors already sell bread nearby, but neither of them opens before nine, so we will serve customers who are currently ignored.
accepted: Our target market is office workers who want fresh bread before eight in the morning. Two competitors already sell bread nearby, but neither of them opens before nine, so we will serve customers who are currently ignored.
Our target customers are people who work in the offices around the bakery. One competitor already sells bread in the area, but it does not open early, so we will offer fresh bread before work.
Our main customers are office workers who buy bread on their way to work. Two competitors already sell bread in the area, but neither opens before nine, which leaves the early morning open to us.

feedback.es: La sección de mercado describe al cliente objetivo, nombra a los competidores y explica qué espacio queda libre.

origin.text: Tu negocio es una panadería nueva en un barrio de oficinas. Escribe la sección de mercado en dos o tres frases: quiénes son tus clientes objetivo, qué competidores hay y qué no cubren.

prompt.es: ¿A qué sección pertenece esta frase y qué deja entrever?

choices.text: Risks: it names a threat and hints that the workshop depends strongly on its suppliers.
Finance: it reports the workshop's cash flow and the size of the loan it needs.
Market: it compares the workshop's prices with those of its competitors.
Operations: it explains how the workshop buys parts from its suppliers each week.

feedback.es: La frase nombra una amenaza (costes que suben) y revela la dependencia de los proveedores: es la sección de riesgos.

origin.text: If the price of parts rises faster than our sales, the workshop could lose money within a year, and it would have to close unless we find a cheaper supplier.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La sección de finanzas muestra cuándo se llega al equilibrio.»

answer.text: The finance section shows when the business will break even

feedback.es: El sujeto es The finance section y when introduce la pregunta indirecta sobre el momento.

prompt.es: ¿Qué fragmento pertenece a la sección de operaciones?

choices.text: Two competitors already repair bicycles within a kilometre of the station.
The workshop will open six days a week, with two shifts on weekdays.
We will promote the opening with posters and a weekly offer for students.
We need a loan to buy tools and cover the first three months of rent.

feedback.es: Días de apertura y turnos describen el funcionamiento diario: es operaciones; los demás fragmentos son mercado, marketing y finanzas.

es: Usar con precisión el vocabulario de un pitch de negocio (scope, stake, leverage, margin, overheads, niche, viable, scale up) apoyado en cifras o razones.

vocabulary.es: viable, que funciona en la práctica
cobrar impulso, empezar a tener aceptación

teaching.en: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood, which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.
teaching.es: El alcance de la primera fase se limita a un barrio, lo que mantiene bajos los gastos fijos mientras los dueños ponen a prueba la idea.
teaching.explanationEs: Scope es hasta dónde llega el proyecto; overheads son los gastos fijos: alquiler, electricidad, seguro.
segments: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood,
which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.
teaching.audioText: The scope of the first phase is limited to one neighbourhood, which keeps overheads low while the owners test the idea.

teaching.en: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop, so she shares both its profits and its losses.
teaching.es: Sara tiene una participación del veinte por ciento en el taller, así que comparte tanto sus beneficios como sus pérdidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Stake es la parte de un negocio que posee alguien; se usa con hold o have.
segments: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop,
so she shares both its profits and its losses.
teaching.audioText: Sara holds a twenty per cent stake in the workshop, so she shares both its profits and its losses.

teaching.en: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.
teaching.es: Podemos aprovechar los contactos de Leo para abrirnos paso en un nicho que las empresas grandes han pasado por alto.
teaching.explanationEs: Leverage es un verbo transitivo (sin of); break into = entrar en un mercado difícil; niche = grupo pequeño y concreto.
segments: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into
a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.
teaching.audioText: We can leverage Leo's contacts to break into a niche that the larger firms have overlooked.

teaching.en: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair, the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.
teaching.es: Con un margen del cuarenta por ciento en cada reparación, el taller puede cobrar impulso incluso en una temporada floja.
teaching.explanationEs: Margin es la diferencia entre precio y coste; gain traction describe una idea que empieza a funcionar.
segments: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair,
the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.
teaching.audioText: With a margin of forty per cent on each repair, the workshop can gain traction even in a slow season.

teaching.en: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.
teaching.es: Cuando el piloto demuestre ser viable, ampliaremos el negocio y nos beneficiaremos de las economías de escala al comprar piezas.
teaching.explanationEs: Viable significa que funciona en la práctica; scale up = ampliar; economies of scale = costes más bajos al crecer.
segments: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up
and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.
teaching.audioText: Once the pilot proves viable, we will scale up and benefit from economies of scale in buying parts.

teaching.en: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.
teaching.es: Conseguir un punto de apoyo en un mercado saturado solo es realista si el nicho está bien definido y el plan es viable.
teaching.explanationEs: A foothold in es el primer apoyo firme en un mercado; se dice a foothold in, no on.
segments: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if
the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.
teaching.audioText: Winning a foothold in a crowded market is realistic only if the niche is clearly defined and the plan is viable.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por ahora, el alcance del proyecto es deliberadamente pequeño.»

feedback.es: Scope es el alcance del proyecto: aquí, un solo barrio.

hint.es: Sustantivo para «hasta dónde llega el proyecto».

origin.text: We will start in a single neighbourhood and open a second workshop only when the first one makes a profit. For now, the ___ of the project is small on purpose.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del pitch usa el término con precisión?

choices.text: We plan to scope Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.
We plan to leverage Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.
We plan to stake Leo's contacts in the cycling clubs to reach our first customers.

feedback.es: Leverage es el verbo para sacar partido de algo que ya se tiene, como contactos; scope y stake son sustantivos.

hint.es: Busca el verbo que significa aprovechar lo que ya tienes.

origin.text: Leo has worked for ten years with the city's cycling clubs, and most of their members do not yet know that our workshop exists.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Sara tiene una participación del treinta por ciento en el taller.»

answer.text: Sara holds a thirty per cent stake in the workshop

feedback.es: Holds a thirty per cent stake expresa la parte del negocio que posee Sara.

hint.es: Hold va con a thirty per cent stake.

prompt.es: Elige el término exacto para cada frase del pitch.

feedback.es: Cada definición apunta a un término: alcance, margen, gastos fijos y nicho.

sentences: The business will only serve one neighbourhood in phase one, so the ___ is small.
Customers pay fifty dollars and the parts cost thirty, so the ___ is twenty dollars on each repair.
Rent, electricity and insurance are the ___ we pay every month, whether we repair one bike or fifty.
No large firm serves this small group of cyclists, so it is a ___ that we can fill.
origin.text: A possible partner has asked Leo to explain four terms in his pitch. Choose the exact word for each sentence: scope, margin, overheads or niche.

prompt.es: ¿Qué conclusión del pitch usa el término con precisión?

choices.text: On these figures the business has a large stake, because income is clearly higher than costs.
On these figures the business is a niche, because income is clearly higher than costs.
On these figures the business is viable, because income is clearly higher than costs.

feedback.es: Viable significa que el negocio funciona en la práctica; que los ingresos superen los costes lo demuestra.

origin.text: Income next year is forecast at ninety thousand dollars, and all costs together come to sixty thousand.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué plan expone la hablante y en qué condiciones.

choices.text: To open a second branch only after the first one steadily makes a profit.
To open a second branch at once, since repeat customers already pay the costs.
To sell shares in the workshop once repeat customers bring a third of the income.

feedback.es: Ampliarán cuando el taller dé beneficios de forma estable, no antes; hasta entonces mantienen el mismo equipo.

origin.audio: The pilot has been running for six months and it has started to gain traction: repeat customers now account for a third of our income. Once the workshop steadily makes a profit, we will scale up and open a second branch, although we will keep the same small team until then.

prompt.es: Elige el término que completa cada frase del pitch.

feedback.es: Participación, aprovechar, ampliar y viable: cada espacio pide el término más preciso del pitch.

sentences: Mia owns thirty per cent of the company, so she has a big ___ in its success.
We will use our good name to win customers: we will ___ our good name.
The pilot worked, so we can now ___ up to three cities.
The figures show that we can earn money: the plan is ___.
origin.text: Pitch to a possible partner: Mia joined the project last year and now owns a share of the company. The pilot branch has covered its costs since May, and the first customers keep coming back. Leo believes that the idea is ready to grow.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué aconseja el inversor.

choices.text: Grow soon, since a fair margin and a sound idea already prove that the niche is real.
Wait to grow until regular customers show that the niche is real.
Accept his investment for a stake now and use the money to grow faster.

feedback.es: Aconseja no ampliar todavía: primero comprobar el nicho con clientes habituales y, si cobra impulso, volver a hablar de la participación; tener buen margen no sustituye esa prueba.

origin.audio: Your overheads are still high, so I would not advise you to scale up yet. First, test whether the niche is really there, and use your contacts to sign two or three regular customers. If the idea starts to gain traction, come back to us, and we will talk about a stake. I have seen many small firms grow too fast and lose the customers who made them successful. You have a sound idea and a fair margin, so there is no need to hurry. Let the numbers show that you can cover your overheads for six months, and the rest will follow.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad del negocio describe este fragmento?

choices.text: A narrow scope, caused by too few partners.
A thin margin, made worse by heavy overheads.
A weak stake, caused by too many partners.
A crowded niche, caused by strong competitors.

feedback.es: Cada venta deja casi nada tras pagar materiales y mano de obra, y el alquiler y los seguros se comen el resto: margen escaso y gastos fijos altos.

origin.text: The firm sells an excellent product, but each sale leaves almost nothing once the cost of materials and work has been paid. Whatever it earns is swallowed by rent, insurance and electricity.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase de pitch: margen, gastos fijos, viabilidad y crecimiento posterior.

answer.text: With a forty per cent margin and low overheads, the plan is viable, and once it gains traction we will scale up.
accepted: With a forty per cent margin and low overheads, the plan is viable, and once it gains traction we will scale up.
The margin is forty per cent and the overheads are low, so the business is viable and we will scale up later.
With a margin of forty per cent and overheads that are low, the idea is viable, and we will scale up when we are ready.

feedback.es: Una buena frase de pitch une cifra y término: margen, gastos fijos, viabilidad y ampliación posterior.

origin.text: Datos: margen del 40 % en cada reparación, gastos fijos bajos gracias a un alquiler económico y un piloto que ya tiene clientes habituales. Escribe una sola frase que exprese viabilidad y un plan de crecimiento posterior.

evidenceGroups: margin of forty per cent on

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud muestra el inversor ante la idea de ampliar el negocio?

choices.text: Enthusiastic, and ready to back the expansion at once if the owners cut their overheads.
Doubtful about the niche itself, and not ready to discuss the plan any further.
Interested, but not ready to back expansion until one workshop proves itself.
Sceptical about the owners, whom he suspects of hiding how high their overheads are.

feedback.es: Le gusta la idea y cree en el nicho, pero quiere ver seis meses de un taller rentable antes de respaldar la ampliación.

origin.text: I like the idea, and I believe the niche is real. What worries me is the order of events: you plan to scale up before you have shown that a single workshop can cover its overheads. Show me six months in which it does, and my doubts will largely disappear.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Podemos aprovechar nuestro buen nombre para llegar a nuevos clientes.»

answer.text: We can leverage our good name to reach new customers

feedback.es: Leverage lleva complemento directo, sin of, y to reach expresa la finalidad.

prompt.es: Completa: «La idea aún no ha cobrado impulso fuera del barrio.»

feedback.es: Gain traction es la colocación habitual para una idea que empieza a tener aceptación.

origin.text: The idea is promising, yet it has not managed to ___ traction among customers outside the neighbourhood.

es: Plantear contingencias con Should + sujeto + verbo base, in the event of / in the event that y failing that, y leer un plan de contingencia sencillo.

vocabulary.es: si eso falla, en su defecto

teaching.en: Should demand fall, we will draw on the cash reserve to pay the rent, and that reserve is our first safeguard.
teaching.es: Si la demanda bajara, recurriremos a la reserva de efectivo para pagar el alquiler, y esa reserva es nuestra primera salvaguarda.
teaching.explanationEs: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if; draw on = recurrir a algo que ya se tiene.
segments: Should demand fall, we will draw on the cash reserve to
pay the rent, and that reserve is our first safeguard.
teaching.audioText: Should demand fall, we will draw on the cash reserve to pay the rent, and that reserve is our first safeguard.

teaching.en: In the event of a supplier delay, we will fall back on a local shop, although its stock is limited.
teaching.es: En caso de retraso del proveedor, recurriremos a una tienda local, aunque sus existencias son limitadas.
teaching.explanationEs: In the event of + sustantivo; fall back on = recurrir a una alternativa segura.
segments: In the event of a supplier delay, we will fall
back on a local shop, although its stock is limited.
teaching.audioText: In the event of a supplier delay, we will fall back on a local shop, although its stock is limited.

teaching.en: A shortfall in sales of two thousand dollars would not close the workshop, because the contingency plan covers it.
teaching.es: Un déficit de ventas de dos mil dólares no cerraría el taller, porque el plan de contingencia lo cubre.
teaching.explanationEs: Shortfall es lo que falta para llegar a una cifra esperada; el plan de contingencia dice qué hacer.
segments: A shortfall in sales of two thousand dollars would not
close the workshop, because the contingency plan covers it.
teaching.audioText: A shortfall in sales of two thousand dollars would not close the workshop, because the contingency plan covers it.

teaching.en: Every major risk needs its own answer, since a knock-on effect can turn a small delay into a large shortfall.
teaching.es: Cada riesgo importante necesita su propia respuesta, porque un efecto en cadena puede convertir un pequeño retraso en un gran déficit.
teaching.explanationEs: Knock-on effect es la consecuencia que provoca otras consecuencias; por eso se planifica por riesgo.
segments: Every major risk needs its own answer, since a knock-on
effect can turn a small delay into a large shortfall.
teaching.audioText: Every major risk needs its own answer, since a knock-on effect can turn a small delay into a large shortfall.

teaching.en: Should stock run out, we will buy parts from a local shop; failing that, we will tell customers to come back tomorrow.
teaching.es: Si se agotaran las existencias, compraremos piezas en una tienda local; si eso falla, pediremos a los clientes que vuelvan mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Failing that introduce el plan B cuando el plan A no funciona; run out = agotarse.
segments: Should stock run out, we will buy parts from a local
shop; failing that, we will tell customers to come back tomorrow.
teaching.audioText: Should stock run out, we will buy parts from a local shop; failing that, we will tell customers to come back tomorrow.

teaching.en: Use the reserve to cushion the blow of a bad winter, but only as a last resort, since a safeguard is not income.
teaching.es: Usa la reserva para amortiguar el golpe de un mal invierno, pero solo como último recurso, porque una salvaguarda no es un ingreso.
teaching.explanationEs: Cushion the blow = reducir el daño de algo; as a last resort = cuando no queda otra opción.
segments: Use the reserve to cushion the blow of a bad winter, but
only as a last resort, since a safeguard is not income.
teaching.audioText: Use the reserve to cushion the blow of a bad winter, but only as a last resort, since a safeguard is not income.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si lloviera toda una semana, ofreceremos recogida a domicilio.»

feedback.es: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if en un registro formal: Should it rain = If it rains.

hint.es: Inversión formal: Should + sujeto + verbo base.

origin.text: The workshop depends on dry weather, so the owners have prepared for the worst. ___ it rain for a whole week, we will offer a home pick-up service.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase formal está bien construida?

choices.text: Should the supplier is late, we will call another one.
Should the supplier will be late, we will call another one.
Should the supplier be late, we will call another one.

feedback.es: Después de Should el verbo va en forma base (be), sin -s ni will.

hint.es: Tras Should el verbo va en forma base.

origin.text: The owners want a formal sentence that means: if the supplier is late, we will call another one.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En caso de un retraso prolongado, avisaremos a los clientes.»

answer.text: In the event of a long delay, we will warn customers
accepted: In the event of a long delay, we will warn customers
In the event of a long delay we will warn customers

feedback.es: In the event of va seguido de un sustantivo (a long delay) y después de la coma va la acción.

hint.es: Empieza por In the event of.

prompt.es: Según el plan, ¿cuál es el último recurso del taller?

choices.text: Asking the bank for a loan.
Shortening the opening hours.
Using the cash reserve to pay the rent.

feedback.es: La inversión «only as a last resort will we ask the bank» indica que el préstamo se deja para cuando nada más funciona.

origin.text: Plan B for a wet autumn: Should rain keep customers away for a week, we will offer a home pick-up service. Failing that, we will shorten our opening hours and use the cash reserve to cover the rent, but only as a last resort will we ask the bank for a loan.

origin.audio: In the event of a shortfall in sales, we will first draw on the cash reserve for three months. Failing that, we will ask the bank for a short loan. A price rise would be the final option, because losing customers could produce a knock-on effect that the workshop could not afford.

prompt.es: Escribe cuatro planes de contingencia breves para tu taller de bicicletas.

answer.text: Should demand fall, we will use our cash reserve and reduce our opening hours. In the event of a supplier delay, we will order parts from a local shop. Should stock run out, we will ask customers to wait. Failing that, we will offer them a discount.
accepted: Should demand fall, we will use our cash reserve and reduce our opening hours. In the event of a supplier delay, we will order parts from a local shop. Should stock run out, we will ask customers to wait. Failing that, we will offer them a discount.

Should sales fall, we will draw on the cash reserve and cut our costs. In the event of a late delivery, we will call another supplier. Should the stock run out, we will borrow parts from a friend's shop. Failing that, we will tell customers to come back tomorrow.

feedback.es: Cada plan necesita una fórmula formal y una acción concreta; el plan B empieza con Failing that.

origin.text: Tienes un taller de bicicletas. Escribe cuatro planes: si baja la demanda (Should…), si el proveedor se retrasa (In the event of…), si se agota el stock (Should…) y un plan B (Failing that,…).

prompt.es: ¿Qué implica el autor con su propuesta de actuar hoy?

choices.text: That the owner is certain the bank will refuse, so the workshop must close.
That waiting until the problem appears would leave too little time to act.

feedback.es: Propone el plan hoy y no en marzo, «when it would already be late»: esperar al problema dejaría poco margen para reaccionar.

origin.text: Note from the owner: The bank has warned us that it may not renew the credit line next year. Should that happen, the cash reserve would cover three months of rent, no more. In the event that sales stay flat, I see no realistic way to last until the end of the year. I am therefore proposing a contingency plan today, not in March, when it would already be late. I would rather be told that I worried too early than that I acted too late. If the credit line is renewed, we will have lost nothing but an afternoon; if it is not, we will have bought ourselves a whole year.

Telling customers to return, because that breaks the promise of the workshop.

title.en: Present the plan for a small business
title.es: Presentar el plan de un pequeño negocio

es: Presentar un plan de arranque para un negocio propio: calendario con plazos, tareas delegadas, un riesgo con su contingencia y respuesta a una objeción.

vocabulary.es: entender su argumento, darle la razón en eso

teaching.en: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.
teaching.es: Gracias por venir; empezaré mi presentación con el calendario y después pasaré a la previsión y a los riesgos.
teaching.explanationEs: Una apertura clara anuncia el orden de la presentación.
segments: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with
the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.
teaching.audioText: Thank you for coming; I will begin my pitch with the timeline, then turn to the forecast and the risks.

teaching.en: We forecast fifty repairs a month by December, and we can back up that figure with two months of real orders.
teaching.es: Prevemos cincuenta reparaciones al mes para diciembre, y podemos respaldar esa cifra con dos meses de pedidos reales.
teaching.explanationEs: Forecast también es verbo; back up = apoyar una afirmación con datos.
segments: We forecast fifty repairs a month by December, and we can
back up that figure with two months of real orders.

teaching.en: An investor may raise an objection that cycling drops in winter, and a fair question deserves a direct answer.
teaching.es: Un inversor puede plantear la objeción de que el ciclismo baja en invierno, y una pregunta razonable merece una respuesta directa.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise an objection = plantear una objeción; fair question = pregunta legítima.
segments: An investor may raise an objection that cycling drops in
winter, and a fair question deserves a direct answer.

teaching.en: I take your point, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan for every major risk.
teaching.es: Entiendo su argumento, pero permítame tranquilizarle: tenemos un plan de contingencia para cada riesgo importante.
teaching.explanationEs: Take your point reconoce la objeción sin rendirse; reassure lleva a la persona como objeto directo.
segments: I take your point, but let me reassure you:
we have a contingency plan for every major risk.
teaching.audioText: I take your point, but let me reassure you: we have a contingency plan for every major risk.

teaching.en: I would like to address your objection briefly, because a realistic plan should stand by its figures.
teaching.es: Me gustaría responder brevemente a su objeción, porque un plan realista debe mantener sus cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Address = abordar una cuestión; stand by = mantener lo dicho cuando se cuestiona.
segments: I would like to address your objection briefly, because
a realistic plan should stand by its figures.

teaching.en: A calm answer backed by data can win over a doubtful investor far more effectively than a long speech.

teaching.explanationEs: Win over = ganarse el apoyo de alguien; la calma y los datos pesan más que la extensión.
segments: A calm answer backed by data can win over a

origin.text: Thank you for the pitch. I liked the timeline and the honesty about winter. My hesitation is the forecast: it rests on two months of orders, both in summer. I am not saying no.
